title: Functoriality of the conormal sheaf of a closed immersion
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ and $i':Z'\to X'$ be closed immersions of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathcal I'=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and call $\mathcal C_{Z/X}:=i^*\mathcal I\;(=i^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2))$ and $\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}:=i'^*\mathcal I'$ their conormal sheaves [def-pc-module-pullback], where $\mathcal I^2$ denotes the subsheaf generated by products of two local sections of $\mathcal I$. Let $g:X\to X'$ and $f:Z\to Z'$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $g\circ i=i'\circ f$. Then (1) the image $\mathcal I'\mathcal O_X$ of $g^*\mathcal I'\to g^*\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is contained in $\mathcal I$, so $g^\sharp$ induces an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\gamma:g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal I$; (2) the composite $c:f^*\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}=f^*i'^*\mathcal I'\cong i^*g^*\mathcal I'\xrightarrow{i^*\gamma}i^*\mathcal I=\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ is a canonical map of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, characterized by: for affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset X'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $g(U)\subset U'$, $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, $Z'\cap U'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'/I')$, the induced map $I'/I'^2=\Gamma(Z'\cap U',\mathcal C_{Z'/X'})\to\Gamma(Z\cap U,\mathcal C_{Z/X})=I/I^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] is induced by $g^\sharp:R'\to R$, which satisfies $g^\sharp(I')\subset I$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R4 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial), case of closed immersions (second and third paragraphs of its proof); the conormal sheaf of a closed immersion is Morphisms, Definition 01R2 (morphisms-definition-conormal-sheaf) and Lemma 01R3 (morphisms-lemma-affine-conormal)

proof.text: *(1) The pulled-back ideal is contained in the ideal of $Z$.* A section of $\mathcal I'$ maps to zero in $i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'}$ by the kernel definition. Pulling this equality around the commutative square $g\circ i=i'\circ f$ shows that its image under $g^\sharp$ restricts to zero on $Z$: on stalks at $z\in Z$, the composite $\mathcal I'_{g(i(z))}\to\mathcal O_{X',g(i(z))}\to\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ equals the map through $\mathcal O_{Z',f(z)}$ and is zero. Hence the image $\mathcal I'\mathcal O_X$ of $g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] lies in $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)=\mathcal I$. Corestricting that map gives the $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\gamma:g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal I$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R4 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial), second paragraph; Schemes, Lemma 01HP (schemes-lemma-characterize-closed-subspace), easy direction

proof.text: *(2) Passage to the conormal sheaves.* Pull $\gamma:g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal I$ from Step (1) back along $i$ to obtain $i^*g^*\mathcal I'\to i^*\mathcal I$. The pullback-composition isomorphism in [def-pc-module-pullback], together with $g\circ i=i'\circ f$, identifies its source with $f^*i'^*\mathcal I'=f^*\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}$ and its target with $i^*\mathcal I=\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. This is the canonical map $c$. Since $g^\sharp$ is multiplicative and Step (1) sends $\mathcal I'$ into $\mathcal I$, it also sends $(\mathcal I')^2$ into $\mathcal I^2$; equivalently the same map is obtained from the conormal quotients $\mathcal I'/(\mathcal I')^2$ and $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, as in Stacks 01R4.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01R4 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial), second paragraph of the proof; Definition 01R2 (morphisms-definition-conormal-sheaf)

proof.text: *(3) Affine description of the induced map.* Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ and $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset X'$ with $g(U)\subset U'$. The closed-immersion affine description [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] identifies $Z\cap U$ and $Z'\cap U'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(R'/I')$, where $I$ and $I'$ are the kernels of the corresponding structure-ring maps. The induced map on affine opens is the ring homomorphism $g^\sharp:R'\to R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and Step (1) gives $g^\sharp(I')\subseteq I$: an element of $I'$ maps to a section whose restriction to $Z$ is zero. Thus $g^\sharp$ induces the well-defined map $I'/I'^2\to I/I^2$, $a+I'^2\mapsto g^\sharp(a)+I^2$, since $g^\sharp(I'^2)\subseteq I^2$.

*(4) Identification with sections and characterization.* The affine conormal calculation [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] identifies the sections on $Z'\cap U'$ and $Z\cap U$ with $I'/I'^2$ and $I/I^2$. Pullback of a section represented by $a\in I'$ followed by $i^*\gamma$ takes it to the class of $g^\sharp(a)$; Step (3) shows this does not depend on the representative. Thus $c$ has the asserted affine description. This description determines $c$: for each $z\in Z$, choose an affine neighbourhood $U'$ of $g(i(z))$ in $X'$, then an affine neighbourhood $U$ of $i(z)$ inside the open $g^{-1}(U')$; the closed immersions make $Z\cap U$ and $Z'\cap U'$ affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. These $Z\cap U$ cover $Z$. Since $\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections], [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives the sections of its pullback on $Z\cap U$ as $(I'/I'^2)\otimes_{R'/I'}(R/I)$; the elements $a\otimes1$ generate this module. Therefore a sheaf map on $Z\cap U$ is determined by its values on the classes $a\in I'/I'^2$, which the affine description fixes, and these local determinations agree on overlaps.
